wrong: Prints item and separator together in the loop, leaving an extra separator at the end. | right: Handle one item outside the loop so n items get n - 1 separators.
wrong: Prints item and separator together in the loop, leaving an extra separator at the end. | right: Handle one item outside the loop so n items get n - 1 separators.

[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: in everyday counting each item 'comes with' its separator (each fence section with a post), so a novice prints item and separator together n times. For n items you need n − 1 separators (or n + 1 posts for n sections), so one item has to be handled outside the loop.

[0] names_the_element (N): Loop idiom: a loop that processes n items with n − 1 separators by handling one item outside the loop ('loop and a half').
[1] states_the_rule (S): Print the first item before the loop, then loop over the rest printing separator then item: `System.out.print(a[0]); for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) System.out.print(", " + a[i]);` (or print item then separator for all but the last).

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Order: the first item is printed once before the loop test. Each pass then tests `i < n`, prints the separator, prints a[i] and increments i, so a separator always comes before an item, never after the last one.
[1] output_prediction (OP): For a = {1, 2, 3} the output is `1, 2, 3`: 3 items and exactly 2 separators, with no leading or trailing separator.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One loop pass prints exactly one separator and one item and increments i by 1. The pre-loop statement prints one item and no separator.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The for loop's bounds must match the handled-outside item: if a[0] is printed before the loop, the loop must start at `i = 1`. Starting at 0 duplicates the first item, and `i <= n` runs past the end.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): An off-by-one error is a loop that runs once too many or too few; a fencepost loop is the correct plan for the case that needs one action more than the other.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan: fencepost / loop-and-a-half plan. It produces separated lists (`1, 2, 3`), joined strings, and drawings of n posts with n − 1 rails.

[0] predict_a_change (C): Invariant: after k passes, the output holds k + 1 items and k separators. Moving the separator after the item inside the loop breaks this and leaves a trailing separator. Swapping the outside item from first to last needs the loop to cover 0 .. n−2 instead.
[1] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: n items need n − 1 separators; one item must be handled outside the loop. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Printing `a[i] + ", "` for every i: the output ends with an extra separator (`1, 2, 3, `). Any n ≥ 1 triggers it.
[2] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use a fencepost loop whenever items are joined by separators or bounded by posts (CSV lines, comma lists, drawings). It is not needed when every item gets the same surrounding text; there, a plain loop is right.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Array indices run from 0 to length − 1; the item handled outside the loop must exist. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: An empty array (n = 0): `print(a[0])` before the loop throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
An off-by-one error is a loop that runs once too many or too few; a fencepost loop is the correct plan for the case that needs one action more than the other.
A fencepost loop is a for loop with one item handled outside it.
